apush-u1-l1.reason: Lesson read end to end as a student. All flagged facts checked against the books: migration 'as far as 40,000 years' confirmed in Princeton ('from as early as 40,000 years ago to as recently as 15,000'); population '1 to 5 million... another 20 million populated Mexico' confirmed verbatim in Princeton; Tenochtitlan 'more populous than any city in Europe' in 1500 confirmed in Princeton; Iroquois League 'formed in the 1400s' confirmed in Barron's ('dates back to perhaps the fifteenth century'); Chaco 'hundreds of rooms' and 'severe drought in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries' dispersing Pueblo from the Four Corners confirmed in Barron's; Chinook longhouses 'contained up to fifty people' confirmed in Barron's; Las Casas 3 million to 200 correctly attributed to Las Casas himself with 'figures contested' (Barron's gives a different figure, over a million to 500, so the lesson's hedging is right). Sections 174/288/165/279/161/296 words, all in 150-300; narrative 1,410 words; no paragraph over 90 words; no trap language; worked items 9/9 prompts and 9/9 model answers verbatim against the bank. NOTES (not fails): (1) the Cahokia-London size comparison appears in none of the three books - standard hedged claim, not contradicted; (2) Waldseemuller, Cantino, and Cronon are not named in the books' chapters - standard facts, primary sources cited; (3) the Inca appear only in worked item 1/the SAQ 0001 stimulus, never in the narrative; (4) the lesson teaches no English-colonization content (see SAQ 0005 note); (5) Powell's Mound photo is a book-page scan (standing quibble); (6) worked item 1 must be re-synced when SAQ 0001 is fixed to 2-sentence model answers.
